title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA
data_curation: Training data comes from a self-improvement loop, not a fixed corpus. Starting from a versioned seed bank, the current model proposes harder task variants (lifting constraints, hidden preferences, chained sub-goals, embedded contradictions). Each must carry a verifiable answer or rubric, and is kept only if well-defined and not already solved reliably. Trajectories run in the production harness, are scored on outcome and process, filtered for invalid runs and duplicates, and the validated, informative ones train the LoRA specialists. Evaluation sets draw on product data: ChatBench's 46 cases are de-identified real conversations flagged by a UX Agent from negative feedback and behavioural anomalies, and LivingBench's 40 scenarios are seeded from product failure taxonomies. The report states it does not document the consent basis, the de-identification audit, or a complete per-specialist training specification.
curriculum: Every model starts from a frozen pretrained base (GLM-5.2 744B for Venti, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B for Tall); only the LoRA specialists are trained. The recursive self-improvement (RSI) loop has three stages per generation. Discovery builds a harder task bank. Expansion runs tasks under a fixed model-plus-harness configuration and searches prompt/skill/tool/hook edits in 'language space'. Update applies GRPO to the adapters from selected trajectories and registers the accepted harness configuration (HCP) as the next generation's. The base, the specialists, and the harness are released on separate schedules. The paper releases one snapshot and does not measure gains across generations. The four specialists share one recipe: AdamW, LR 5e-6, batch 4, 4 epochs, linear-warmup cosine schedule with warmup 0.1. Agent (L1) uses 1 epoch; GenUI (L3) uses batch 2 and 1 epoch.
method: Mixture-of-LoRA (MoL): a frozen base plus four specialist LoRAs (L0 Chat, L1 Agent, L2 Coding, L3 GenUI). Venti adapters are rank 16, alpha 32, about 7.69B stored values each; Tall adapters are rank 64, alpha 128. Each user turn goes through a Proxy loop: L0 routes by emitting one label under a constrained grammar (24-token budget, no separate router model), the chosen specialist answers from its own conversation view, then writes a summary of at most 192 tokens that other adapters inherit. Stable per-adapter views make LoRA-aware prefix-cache reuse happen automatically. The harness is co-designed and itself treated as a training target: UI4A (component-native React GenUI), a stateful REPL agent harness that keeps intermediate values in a persistent namespace and promotes only validated reusable helpers, and the versioned TOML Harness Context Protocol (HCP). MindForge orchestrates the RSI loop and MinT exports versioned adapter revisions. LongStraw replays responses only, without backprop through the prompt, for 2M-token RL. To reduce rollout/learner mismatch on sparse MoE and DSA bases, it uses R3 routing replay, DSA implementation alignment, and IcePop-style token masking.
eval_metrics: Internal Personal Intelligence benchmarks: Macaron ChatBench (46 cases, GLM-5.2 judge with six fixed axioms plus persona/scenario conditioning, 1-5 score, 3 samples) and LivingBench (40 simulated scenarios with at most 10 turns and four noise types; score = 0.7 x need fulfilment + 0.3 x process quality). UI4A-Bench: 161 cases, Final Score from five weighted Layer Scores. External: VitaBench, VitaBench2 (Avg@1), tau3-Bench (pass@1), PinchBench (best run), ClawGym (pass@1), SWE-Verified, TerminalBench 2.1 (pass@1), DeepSWE (best of 3), and SWE Atlas QnA (pass@3), the coding rows run with the Claude Code scaffold; some baseline cells are imported from public leaderboards. Venti scores: ChatBench 58.3 (GPT-5.5 55.5), LivingBench 64.0 (Opus 4.8 63.8), UI4A-Bench 87.8 (Opus 4.8 75.9), TerminalBench 2.1 87.6, SWE-Verified 85.6 (Opus 4.8 88.6), DeepSWE 58.4 (GPT-5.5 70.0). Routing accuracy 99.12% on a 6,448-sample trace drawn from training data.
key_results: Macaron-V1-Venti leads the compared frontier models on ChatBench (58.3), LivingBench (64.0), UI4A-Bench (87.8 vs 75.9 for Opus 4.8) and TerminalBench 2.1 (87.6), but trails on VitaBench, ClawGym, SWE-Verified, DeepSWE and SWE Atlas QnA. Macaron-V1-Tall beats its Qwen3.6-35B-A3B base on all seven matched rows (e.g. UI4A-Bench 59.3 vs 33.9). Separately, with the GLM-5.2 base frozen and no weight updates, adaptive harness-configuration search eventually passes all 122 TerminalBench-derived tasks the base had failed, whereas the best single full-set configuration passed 11/122. MoL stores about 74% fewer parameters than four replicated merged-base copies.
evolution_note: Macaron-V1 builds on LoRA (including Thinking Machines' 'LoRA without regret'), multi-tenant LoRA serving (Punica, S-LoRA), GRPO, and its own earlier Macaron-V1-Preview and Macaron-A2UI work. It reacts to the cross-task interference and static-checkpoint limits of monolithic post-training. It shifts post-training toward an agent system with separately versioned base, adapters, and harness, where harness search ('language space') and adapter RL are coupled. It positions MoL as an interoperability contract for continual learning and for composing specialists from different teams. The authors state that compounding gains across generations and collective-intelligence benefits are not yet demonstrated.
